spec.summary: Bring an AI coding agent into every Kubernetes cluster you manage — without leaving Freelens.
Talk to your cluster in natural language with an AI agent that reads, explains and, with your approval, changes resources.
spec.description:
Freelens AI brings a chat with an AI agent into Freelens, with one
conversation per cluster. The agent reads, explains and, with your
approval, changes Kubernetes resources, while the chat keeps the full
context of the conversation.

The extension is a client of a large language model API: it talks the
OpenAI Chat Completions and Responses APIs, to OpenAI directly or to any
endpoint that implements them, such as an OpenAI-compatible gateway. You
bring your own API key, and the provider bills you per token.

- **Cluster operations through tools**: list, get, create, update, patch
  and delete any resource kind, CRDs included, read pod logs, resize pods
  in place, scale and restart workloads, and analyze warning events.
- **Human in the loop**: every change is shown as YAML for review and
  applied only after you approve it, with the current state of the
  resource kept, so that a change can be reverted.
- **MCP agent**: MCP servers, configured per cluster, run in Freelens and
  reach the cluster the chat is open for.
- **Persistent sessions**: the transcript survives restarts, with a live
  token counter and cost estimate.

spec.summary: Dashboard, lists and details of the FluxCD resources, with actions to reconcile, suspend and resume them.
spec.description:
Support for [FluxCD](https://fluxcd.io/), the continuous and progressive
delivery solutions for Kubernetes that keep the cluster state in sync with
sources such as Git repositories, OCI artifacts and Helm charts.

The extension provides a dashboard, cluster pages, list views and detail
panels for the FluxCD custom resources of the `fluxcd.controlplane.io`,
`source.toolkit.fluxcd.io`, `source.extensions.fluxcd.io`,
`kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io`, `helm.toolkit.fluxcd.io`,
`image.toolkit.fluxcd.io` and `notification.toolkit.fluxcd.io` API groups.
The detail view shows the status conditions, the spec fields and the
related objects. The menu of a resource reconciles, suspends and resumes
it. While the extension is enabled, these resources are listed once, under
"FluxCD", and left out of the Custom Resources tree of the sidebar.

## Requirements

- Kubernetes >= 1.24
- Flux >= 2.0.0
- flux-operator >= 0.6.0

spec.summary: A Claude-powered chat per cluster that drives your own Claude Code installation with permission-gated Kubernetes tools.
spec.description:
Freelens for Claude embeds a Claude-powered chat in Freelens, with one
conversation per cluster. Claude answers questions about the selected
cluster and can act on it, but only through a set of typed,
permission-gated Kubernetes tools, never through an unrestricted shell.

The extension is a frontend to your own Claude Code installation. There is
no provider selection and no API key to store: it spawns the Claude Code
binary already installed on your machine and inherits whatever
authentication it uses, so billing is whatever your Claude Code uses. The
extension never sees your credentials.

This is a community project, not an official Anthropic product. The name
uses the "Claude" trademark nominatively to describe what the extension
works with; it does not imply endorsement by or affiliation with
Anthropic.

## Requirements

- Claude Code installed and logged in: run `claude` once in a terminal to
  authenticate.

spec.summary: Overview, lists and details of the standard and experimental resources of the Kubernetes Gateway API.
spec.description:
Support for the [Kubernetes Gateway API](https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/),
the official Kubernetes project of expressive, extensible and role-oriented
interfaces for service networking, designed as the successor to the Ingress
API.

The extension adds a "Gateway API" entry to the cluster menu, for the
standard and experimental resources of the `gateway.networking.k8s.io` and
`gateway.networking.x-k8s.io` API groups:

- **Overview**: one pie chart per installed kind with the number of objects
  that are Ready, Not Ready, In Progress or Unknown, filtered by namespace,
  and the events of the Gateway API objects.
- **One list per kind**, with sort and search, in the newest API version
  the cluster serves.
- **Details** of every kind and version: the status conditions, the spec
  fields and links to the referenced objects.
- **One sidebar entry per kind**: the Gateway API kinds are listed once,
  under "Gateway API", and left out of the Custom Resources tree.

## Requirements

- Kubernetes >= 1.26
- The Gateway API CRDs installed in the cluster

spec.summary: Freelens extension for Kamaji, the Kubernetes Control Plane Manager.
A visual interface to watch what Karpenter does to the nodes of a cluster, on AWS, Azure and GCP.
spec.description:
Support for [Karpenter](https://karpenter.sh/), the open source node
autoscaler that launches and removes the nodes of a Kubernetes cluster to
fit its pods. The extension reads the Karpenter objects, the nodes, the
pods and the events of the cluster, and writes nothing to it.

It adds **Karpenter** to the cluster sidebar:

- **Overview**: a dashboard with the nodes and their status, one card per
  NodePool with its node class, instance types, limits, usage of CPU and
  memory, its nodes and its recent events, and a filter by name, node
  status, instance type and NodePool status.
- **Node Claims**, **Node Pools** and **Node Overlays**, and the node
  classes of the cloud: **EC2 Node Classes** on AWS, **AKS Node Classes**
  on Azure, and **GCE Node Classes** and **GCE Custom Machine Types** on
  GCP, as lists with their details.
- A Karpenter section in the details of a node.

It follows the Freelens theme, light or dark, and updates while it is open,
as Karpenter launches and removes nodes.

spec.summary: Displays Kubernetes resources and their relations as a real-time force-directed graph.
Lists and details of the ValsSecret and DbSecret resources of vals-operator, which syncs secrets from vals backends.
spec.description:
Support for [vals-operator](https://github.com/digitalis-io/vals-operator),
the Kubernetes operator that syncs secrets from the backends of
[vals](https://github.com/helmfile/vals), such as HashiCorp Vault, AWS
Secrets Manager or GCP Secret Manager, into Kubernetes `Secret`s.

The extension adds a "Vals" entry to the cluster sidebar, with a list page
and a details panel for each of the operator's resources:

- **Vals Secrets**: the `Secret` that a `ValsSecret` writes, the `ref` of
  every data source, the templates, the rollout targets, the conditions,
  and a "Refresh" action that asks the operator to read the backend again.
- **DB Secrets**: the `Secret` that a `DbSecret` writes, the Vault mount
  and role that issue its credentials, and whether the operator renews
  their lease.

Of the objects that the operator writes, the extension reads the metadata
only: it never reads the data of a `Secret`, and shows the reference of a
secret, never its value.

spec.summary: See expire date from certificates inside Kubernetes secrets.
Field-based filtering for any Kubernetes resource kind, including CRDs, with per-kind persistence and saved filter sets.
